title: CPUThrottlingHigh
body:
**Likely root cause:** The container 'sftp' in pod cm-000000000000-ztp-76b95f8d4d-g77z2 (namespace cm-default-production) has its CPU limit set too low for its current workload, causing 52.71% of its CPU cycles to be throttled by the CFS quota.

**Suggested remediation:**
- Inspect current CPU requests/limits vs. actual usage: `kubectl -n cm-default-production describe pod cm-000000000000-ztp-76b95f8d4d-g77z2` and check `kubectl top pod -n cm-default-production`.
- If usage is legitimately near/above the limit, raise the container's CPU limit (and request if needed) via the workload manifest / Helm values and roll out the change.
- If the increase isn't warranted, verify no runaway process in the sftp container is consuming unexpected CPU (exec in and check top/ps).
- Confirm throttling drops after the change by re-checking the CPUThrottlingHigh metric for this pod/container.

annotations.description: 52.71% throttling of CPU in namespace cm-default-production for container sftp in pod cm-000000000000-ztp-76b95f8d4d-g77z2 on cluster .

title: PrometheusNotConnectedToAlertmanagers
body:
**Likely root cause:** The Prometheus pod (prometheus-kube-prometheus-stack-prometheus-0) has lost connectivity to or is misconfigured against its Alertmanager endpoints, so it cannot forward alerts.

**Suggested remediation:**
- Confirm scope: verify from the Prometheus pod whether Alertmanager endpoints are reachable (e.g., check the configured alertmanager service DNS/port from the same namespace). 
- Check Alertmanager pod/service health in monitoring namespace; if Alertmanager pods are down or not Ready, restore them first. 
- Inspect the Prometheus config/alertmanager secret for correct endpoint/namespace; re-apply the Prometheus CR or secret if the config drifted. 
- As a low-risk recovery, rolling-restart the Prometheus pod (delete pod prometheus-kube-prometheus-stack-prometheus-0) so it re-establishes the Alertmanager connection. 
- If monitoring is business-critical and the issue persists, treat as lost alerting coverage and notify the monitoring owner.

annotations.description: Prometheus monitoring/prometheus-kube-prometheus-stack-prometheus-0 is not connected to any Alertmanagers.
annotations.summary: Prometheus is not connected to any Alertmanagers.

title: LLMServerCrashLooping
body:
**Likely root cause:** The vLLM container in pod chat-llm-cdf9dc6ff-bgjrf is entering a CrashLoopBackOff state, indicating it is failing to start or immediately exiting after initialization.

**Suggested remediation:**
- Check pod logs via `kubectl logs chat-llm-cdf9dc6ff-bgjrf -n llm-serving --previous` to identify OOMKilled errors, missing weights, or CUDA initialization failures.
- Verify resource requests/limits; if OOMKilled, consider increasing memory limits or reducing batch size in config.
- If logs show configuration errors, review the ConfigMap/Secret mounted to the pod for syntax or connectivity issues (e.g., model repo path).
- If transient, monitor for auto-recovery; if persistent, drain node or delete pod to force rescheduling to a healthy node.

annotations.summary: chat-llm (vLLM) is crash-looping and not serving

title: KubeDeploymentReplicasMismatch
body:
**Likely root cause:** The 'chat-llm' Deployment in the 'llm-serving' namespace is failing to scale to its desired replica count within a 15-minute window, likely due to pod scheduling failures, image pull errors, or resource constraint denials.

**Suggested remediation:**
- Verify current status and recent events for the `chat-llm` pods in the `llm-serving` namespace (`kubectl get pods -n llm-serving -l app=chat-llm -w` and `kubectl describe pod <pod-name> -n llm-serving`).
- Check for ImagePullBackOff, CrashLoopBackOff, or Pending (Insufficient Resources) statuses.
- If caused by transient resource pressure or scheduler issues, manually scale down and up the deployment (`kubectl scale deployment chat-llm -n llm-serving --replicas=0` followed by restoring desired replicas) or restart affected pods.

annotations.description: Deployment llm-serving/chat-llm has not matched the expected number of replicas for longer than 15 minutes on cluster .
annotations.summary: Deployment has not matched the expected number of replicas.

title: KubePodNotReady
body:
**Likely root cause:** The pod `chat-llm-cdf9dc6ff-bgjrf` is stuck in a non-ready state for >15 minutes, likely due to a failed container image pull, a hanging liveness/readiness probe, or a container crash loop (OOMKilled or application error).

**Suggested remediation:**
- Check pod status and events via `kubectl describe pod chat-llm-cdf9dc6ff-bgjrf -n llm-serving` to identify ImagePullBackOff, CrashLoopBackOff, or probe failure messages.
- Review recent logs via `kubectl logs chat-llm-cdf9dc6ff-bgjrf -n llm-serving --previous` (if restart occurred) to catch application-level errors or OOM events.
- If the pod is stuck due to resource constraints or transient errors, attempt a safe restart by deleting the pod to trigger a redeployment: `kubectl delete pod chat-llm-cdf9dc6ff-bgjrf -n llm-serving`.
- If deletion causes repeated crashes, rollback recent changes to the `chat-llm` deployment or image tag.

annotations.description: Pod llm-serving/chat-llm-cdf9dc6ff-bgjrf has been in a non-ready state for longer than 15 minutes on cluster .
annotations.summary: Pod has been in a non-ready state for more than 15 minutes.

title: KubePodCrashLooping
body:
**Likely root cause:** The vLLM container in pod chat-llm-cdf9dc6ff-bgjrf is repeatedly failing to start or crashing immediately after startup within the llm-serving namespace.

**Suggested remediation:**
- Check pod events and logs for the root failure: `kubectl -n llm-serving logs chat-llm-cdf9dc6ff-bgjrf -c vllm --previous` or `kubectl describe pod chat-llm-cdf9dc6ff-bgjrf -n llm-serving`
- Verify if the model weights path or volume mounts are accessible and correctly configured for the vLLM container.
- If the container is OOMKilled, increase memory limits in the Deployment/StatefulSet spec.
- Restart the pod if the issue is transient: `kubectl -n llm-serving delete pod chat-llm-cdf9dc6ff-bgjrf`

annotations.description: Pod llm-serving/chat-llm-cdf9dc6ff-bgjrf (vllm) is in waiting state (reason: "CrashLoopBackOff") on cluster .
